clue.text: Allow poster at motorway junction

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, shortened to AD
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, read here as the letters MI
a T-junction gives the letter T

explanation.surface: Permission sought to put up a billboard at a motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone in is to let them enter, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Find a cafe otherwise engaged

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Locate a coffee shop that is not busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' looks like 'busy', but it means betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be betrothed is to have pledged to marry.

clue.text: Some might say this bird is under age

indicators.note: some might say means a word is spoken that resembles another

parts.note: a minor is someone under age

explanation.surface: People claim this feathered creature is too young.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: This starling relative from Asia is known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Come across the skill that turns to poetry

indicators.note: turns means art is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Encounter the talent that drifts into writing poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross over something is a synonym, as in crossing a mountain range.

clue.text: He examines complaints of graft by Serjeant-Major in the Gulf

indicators.note: in places the graft and the sergeant-major inside the Gulf state

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Persian Gulf
in gardening a bud is grafted onto a stock, so graft can mean bud
SM is the standard abbreviation for sergeant-major

explanation.surface: An inspector looks into corruption involving a senior soldier stationed in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graft' suggests corruption, but it is the horticultural sense: budding is a kind of grafting.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to investigate grievances against public bodies is exactly this role.

clue.text: He wants man to make a seat

definitions.text: He wants man to make a seat

parts.words: He wants man to make a seat
parts.note: a man's name that, with man added after it, gives a cushioned seat

explanation.walkthrough: Add MAN to the German man's name and you get the low upholstered seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A common German forename becomes an upholstered footstool once man is added.

clue.text: Player needs deception in this game

parts.note: a back is a player in football or rugby
gammon is old slang for humbug or deception

explanation.surface: A gambler needs to bluff in this board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests someone at the board, but it is a defender in football or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two with dice and counters.

clue.text: Terminal round southern end of escarpment face

indicators.note: round puts the face around the other letters

parts.note: a dial is a clock face

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of escarpment

explanation.surface: A railway terminus near the southern end of a cliff face.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the word describes the part furthest from the centre, the far end.

clue.text: Spoil a tune composed for Harriet

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: composed means the letters of a tune are put together differently

parts.note: the fodder as printed, a tune, plus the I the setter must have meant, since the anagram needs six letters

explanation.surface: Ruin a melody written for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder is one I short: MAR plus an anagram of A TUNE gives only eight letters. Harriet Martineau was a Victorian writer and social theorist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer and sociologist Harriet bore this surname.

clue.text: Artist leaves backward class in the South of France

indicators.note: leaves means the artist departs from the word
backward means class is read in reverse

parts.note: a seminar is a class
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter quits a remedial class in Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns SEMINAR into RANIMES; 'leaves' then removes RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimes is a city in the south of France known for its Roman arena.

clue.text: "By thinking on — summer's heat" (Richard 11)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shakespeare's Richard II, where Bolingbroke scorns imagining summer heat in the snow

explanation.walkthrough: Richard 11 is the printed form of Richard II. The full line is 'By thinking on the ___ summer's heat', from Act 1 scene 3.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective means imaginary or fanciful, the sense Shakespeare gives the word.

clue.text: Tussle with half-back

definitions.meaning: add the word half and you get the rugby back who feeds the set piece

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the scrum-half is a back, so this word 'with half' makes a back.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly scuffle is a common figurative sense, and in rugby the scrum-half is a position among the backs.

clue.text: Samara has corrected the solution

indicators.note: corrected means the letters of has are put right in a new order

parts.note: a key is the solution to a puzzle or code

explanation.surface: A woman named Samara has fixed the answer to a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Samara' looks like a woman's name, but it is the botanical term for a winged seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A samara is the winged fruit of trees such as the ash, sometimes called by this name.

clue.text: Saint appears at one in using conversion

indicators.note: conversion here means the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A holy figure emerges at a single point in a process of change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges AT, I and USING together.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ignatius of Loyola founded the Jesuits; the name belongs to several saints.

clue.text: Plant has pig on order

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
the Order of the Thistle is a Scottish order of chivalry

explanation.surface: A garden plant has a pig standing on it, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is not a command: it is the Order of the Thistle, Scotland's chivalric order.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed with yellow flowers and milky sap.

clue.text: School accommodation where many a girl lodges

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a lass is a girl
to lodge is to room, live in rented quarters

explanation.surface: A hostel where numerous young women board.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching spaces are the rooms a school provides for its classes.

clue.text: Part of the Indian summer of a saint?

definitions.text: Part of the Indian summer of a saint?

parts.words: Part of the Indian summer of a saint?
parts.note: a summer month with 'in E' added for the Indian part makes a saint's name

explanation.walkthrough: A late-summer month, followed by IN E, gives the saint's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Augustine of Hippo, or of Canterbury, is the saint in question.

clue.text: Shut up this house?

definitions.meaning: put before house this word makes a top-floor flat

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition invites you to complete a compound: this + house.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means confined, and a penthouse is the luxury flat on a building's top floor.

clue.text: For a change tried a tin of colour

indicators.note: for a change means the letters of tried a tin are altered

explanation.surface: Try a can of paint for something different.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright auburn shade named after the Venetian painter who used it for hair.

clue.text: Shakespearian character of oriental enchantment

parts.note: E stands for east, so oriental
glamour originally meant a magic spell

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare role full of Eastern mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Eglamour is a minor character in The Two Gentlemen of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Eglamour helps Silvia escape in The Two Gentlemen of Verona.

clue.text: Nasty cracks in Schliemann's work

definitions.meaning: Heinrich Schliemann excavated Troy, so his work was excavations

explanation.definitionFit: Barbs are jibes made at someone, and archaeological excavations are known informally by the same word.

clue.text: Vigorous legal action tricky to play with

parts.note: vigorous means strong
a lawsuit is a legal action

explanation.surface: A forceful lawsuit proves awkward to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a player wins tricks with a long holding in one suit, hence 'tricky to play with'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, high-ranking holding in one suit lets a card player take tricks, and figuratively means a forte.

clue.text: French "Homo sapiens"?

parts.note: the Latin means wise man, and the French word for knowing gives a learned person

explanation.walkthrough: Savant is French for 'knowing', and in English a learned person.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned scholar, as the Latin species name means wise man.

clue.text: Huns' leader is the terror of Spain

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: panic is sudden terror

explanation.surface: Attila was the scourge of Iberia.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people or things relating to the Iberian country and its language.

clue.text: What's the matter with the soil? Hydrogen and uranium, to sum up

definitions.text: What's the matter with the soil?

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word sum is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A farmer asks what is wrong with his land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SUM into MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposed organic material forms the dark fertile part of earth.

clue.text: Plant a fool in US agency

indicators.note: in puts the fool inside the US agency

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot has been placed inside American intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb about spies, but it defines the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is a genus of shrubs and trees, one of which yields senna.

clue.text: Hindu holy man had us confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of had us are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sage from India has baffled us.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic who has renounced worldly life in Hinduism.

clue.text: Setting for Excelsior in a special psychiatric unit

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the words special psychiatric

explanation.surface: The location of a hotel called Excelsior is a psychiatric unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's poem Excelsior follows a youth climbing through these mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's poem Excelsior is set among the Swiss mountains.

clue.text: In London farewell to this, Mozart's first opera

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Mozart's

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: Bidding goodbye to Mozart's earliest stage work in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Vale is Latin for farewell; Maida Vale is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding the Latin word for goodbye after it names a district of west London.

clue.text: It's asking a lot to alter arrangement about title

indicators.note: about places the title around which the rearranged letters sit
arrangement means the letters of alter are rearranged

parts.note: Lord is a title

explanation.surface: Rearranging a nobleman's title is a demanding job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' gives TALER as the anagram, and 'about' wraps it round the title; 'It's asking a lot' is the whole-phrase definition, not a cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult demand is an idiom for something that is hard to achieve.

clue.text: Hounds not so much in ecstasy, say, on such a day?

indicators.note: say signals that sent is heard as a word spelt differently

parts.note: to be sent is to be transported with delight
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs are not quite so thrilled on a certain day.
explanation.walkthrough: Hounds are less 'sent' when they cannot pick up a smell; 'Hounds' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A day with no smell for hounds to follow is one without odour.

clue.text: Canon causes parliamentarian to lose his head

indicators.note: to lose means the following words are taken out

parts.note: Roundheads were supporters of Parliament in the English Civil War
the word head itself is removed

explanation.surface: A churchman makes an MP lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests a clergyman, but it is the musical form. Roundheads were Parliament's side in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon in music is a piece where voices enter in turn with the same melody, like a catch.
